title: Elementary chains: unions that preserve first-order truth
summary: Take unions of elementary chains without changing first-order truth at old parameters, and distinguish this from one-way preservation in substructures.
abstract: Can we build a larger model by repeatedly adjoining elements without changing what its formulas say about the elements already present? Tarski's elementary chain theorem says that taking the union preserves these truths: if each inclusion preserves all first-order formulas with parameters, every stage is an elementary submodel of the union. The actual inclusions matter. Repeatedly adding a new least element to the natural-number order gives isomorphic stages, yet their union has no least element. This contrast also highlights what ordinary substructures preserve: universal formulas pass down to smaller domains, while existential formulas pass up to larger ones.
